title: A Day of Very Low Probability

blocks.tex: Only as Harry stumped out the back door, into the back garden, did it occur to him that if an owl \emph{did} come down and snatch the letter, he was going to have some trouble telling Dad about it.
blocks.text: Only as Harry stumped out the back door, into the back garden, did it occur to him that if an owl did come down and snatch the letter, he was going to have some trouble telling Dad about it.

blocks.tex: \emph{But—well—that can’t \emph{really} happen, can it? No matter what my brain seems to believe. If an owl really comes down and grabs this envelope, I’m going to have worries a lot more important than what Dad thinks.}

blocks.tex: Harry took a deep breath, and raised the envelope into the air.

blocks.tex: Calling out \emph{Letter for Hogwarts!} while holding an envelope high in the air in the middle of your own back garden was…actually pretty embarrassing, now that he thought about it.

blocks.tex: \emph{No. I’m better than Dad. I will use the scientific method even if it makes me feel stupid.}

blocks.tex: “Letter—” Harry said, but it actually came out as more of a whispered croak.

blocks.tex: Harry steeled his will, and shouted into the empty sky, “\emph{Letter for Hogwarts! Can I get an owl?}”

blocks.tex: “Harry?” asked a bemused woman’s voice, one of the neighbours.

blocks.tex: Harry pulled down his hand like it was on fire and hid the envelope behind his back like it was drug money. His whole face was hot with shame.
